anomalies.observed: J4 is drawn as an AVR-ISP-6 header, but its MISO pin is connected to the PWM net (U2.6/U3.6) and its MOSI pin is connected to the SDA net (U2.5/U3.5). The ATtiny MISO pin (PB3, labeled TACH on U2.2/U3.2) and MOSI pin (PB5, labeled RST on U2.1/U3.1) are not connected to the header's MISO/MOSI pins.
anomalies.expected: An AVR-ISP-6 programming header should connect MISO to the MCU MISO pin and MOSI to the MCU MOSI pin (for ATtiny45/ATtiny13, PB3/TACH and PB5/RST respectively), so the MCU can be programmed via ISP.

evidence.quote: J4 AVR-ISP-6: pin 1 MISO -> PWM; pin 4 MOSI -> SDA; pin 5 SCK -> SCK; pin 6 RST -> RST (page 1, central/right area)
U2/U3 pin labels: pin 2 XTAL1/PB3 TACH, pin 1 RESET/PB5 RST, pin 6 PWM, pin 5 SDA (page 2, right tile)

anomalies.impact: A standard AVR ISP programmer connected to J4 would not communicate with the ATtiny; programming/reprogramming via the header would fail, and the programmer's MOSI output would drive the I2C SDA net.

parsed.summary: The schematic shows a wiring error on the AVR-ISP-6 header: its MISO/MOSI pins are connected to PWM/SDA instead of the MCU's MISO/MOSI pins, so the intended programming interface is not correctly connected.
